name: Secretin
route: Single injection into a vein over one minute during a diagnostic test
status: FDA-approved (2004) as a diagnostic aid for pancreatic function, gastrinoma and locating duct openings during ERCP
mechanism: Copy of the gut hormone secretin, which makes the pancreas pour out bicarbonate-rich fluid and makes gastrinomas release a burst of gastrin

article.summary: Secretin (ChiRhoStim) is a synthetic copy of a gut hormone used in diagnostic tests of pancreatic function and gastrinoma. It is FDA-approved for testing only and did not help autism in trials.
article.takeaway: Secretin was the first hormone ever discovered, in 1902: the small intestine releases it when acid arrives from the stomach, and it tells the pancreas to send out bicarbonate to neutralize that acid. The synthetic human version, ChiRhoStim, is given once by IV during specialized tests.[^1] It helps measure how well the pancreas works and can unmask a gastrinoma, a gastrin-making tumor, which responds with a sharp gastrin rise that most other conditions do not.[^2] In the late 1990s it was promoted for autism, but randomized trials found **no benefit**.[^3][^4]
glance: Pancreatic function testing, gastrinoma diagnosis, finding duct openings during ERCP
One IV injection over a minute, followed by fluid or blood sampling
Large diagnostic studies of gastrin testing; randomized trials (negative) in autism

blocks.text: Secretin is a 27-amino-acid hormone made by S cells in the upper small intestine. When acidic stomach contents arrive, secretin signals the pancreatic ducts to release water and bicarbonate, which neutralizes the acid and protects the gut lining.

Gastrinomas behave differently. These tumors, usually in the pancreas or duodenum, carry secretin receptors, so a dose of secretin makes them dump extra gastrin into the blood. Normal gastrin-producing cells usually do not respond this way, which is what makes the test useful.[^2]

items: **Pancreatic function:** after secretin, fluid collected from the duodenum is checked for bicarbonate; a peak below 80 mEq/L suggests the pancreas is not working normally, as in chronic pancreatitis
**Gastrinoma:** blood gastrin is measured before and after the dose; a rise above about 110 pg/mL over baseline is strongly suspicious
**ERCP:** the burst of pancreatic juice helps endoscopists find the main and accessory duct openings so they can pass instruments[^1]

blocks.text: A prospective National Institutes of Health study of 293 patients with Zollinger-Ellison syndrome found that 97-99% showed a gastrin rise after secretin or calcium. A rise of at least 120 pg/mL had the best balance of accuracy, detecting 94% of cases with no false positives in that analysis.[^2]

For autism, a 1999 trial in 60 children found no improvement over placebo after a single dose.[^3] A Cochrane review of trials involving more than 900 children reached the same conclusion and advised that secretin should not be given for autism.[^4]

Secretin is injected into a vein over one minute: 0.2 mcg/kg for pancreatic testing and ERCP, and 0.4 mcg/kg for gastrinoma testing.[^1] Some medicines distort results. Anticholinergic drugs can blunt the response, while acid reducers such as H2 blockers and proton pump inhibitors can cause a false gastrin rise, so the testing team gives specific instructions about stopping them beforehand.

Side effects are uncommon and mild. Among 531 people in the label's safety data, the most frequent were nausea, vomiting, flushing and stomach upset, each reported by only a handful of patients.[^1] People with liver disease may over-respond, which can hide pancreatic disease, so results are interpreted in context.

evidence.label: Established diagnostic use; ineffective for autism
evidence.text: Secretin's diagnostic value for gastrinoma rests on large prospective series.[^2] Multiple randomized trials, summarized by Cochrane, show it does not improve autism symptoms.[^4]

faq.a: No. Despite strong interest in the late 1990s, randomized trials found no benefit over placebo, and a Cochrane review advises against using it for autism.[^3][^4]

faq.q: Why do I need to stop my acid reflux medicine before a secretin test?
faq.a: Acid reducers raise gastrin and can make the test look positive for gastrinoma when it is not. The care team will say how long to stop them, if it is safe to do so.[^1]
Some centers give secretin during MRI of the pancreatic ducts to make them easier to see. That use is not listed on the US label.
